main.node: Merge BOM Result With Order Context

nodes.name: Split Order Items
nodes.notes: Splits the 'items' array into one item per node execution, one per product in the order.

nodes.name: Query Tally Stock
nodes.notes: EDIT: Replace the URL with your Tally machine's IP and port (see design doc section 1).

nodes.name: Parse Tally XML
nodes.notes: Converts Tally's XML response into a JSON object n8n can work with.

nodes.name: Compute Shortfall
nodes.notes: EDIT: The path to CLOSINGBALANCE below is a starting guess - confirm the real path once you see Tally's actual XML response and adjust.

nodes.name: Call BOM Explode
nodes.notes: Calls this same workflow's 'When Called by Order Processing' entry point. Pass itemName = product, qtyNeeded = shortfall.

nodes.name: Merge Results
nodes.notes: Append mode: combines the 'enough stock' branch and the 'BOM explode' branch back into one stream. Only one branch ever has data, since they come from an IF, so append just passes through whichever ran.

nodes.name: Deduct Stock In Tally
nodes.notes: EDIT: Same Tally IP/port as the stock query node above.

nodes.name: Log To Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Requires a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential attached in the n8n UI (not stored in this export).

nodes.name: When Called by Order Processing
nodes.notes: Receives itemName, qtyNeeded, orderNumber from whichever workflow called this one (either Order Processing, or this same workflow calling itself).

nodes.name: Nothing Needed
nodes.notes: Enough stock exists for this item, nothing to purchase or manufacture.

nodes.name: Lookup BOM Rows
nodes.notes: Filters the BOM sheet tab for rows matching this item's name. Requires the Google Sheets credential attached in the n8n UI.

nodes.name: Calculate Raw Material Needs
nodes.notes: Multiplies each BOM row's 'Qty Per Unit' by the shortfall to get the actual amount of each raw material needed for this item.

nodes.name: Call Self Recursively
nodes.notes: Calls this same workflow again, now treating the raw material as the new 'item'. This is what makes the BOM explosion go arbitrarily deep.

nodes.name: Merge Recursion Branches
nodes.notes: Append mode: combines results from the 'call self' branch and the 'add to purchase list' branch, only one of which has data per item.

nodes.name: Query Tally Stock1
nodes.notes: EDIT: Replace with your Tally machine IP and port.

nodes.name: Compute Shortfall1
nodes.notes: EDIT: confirm the CLOSINGBALANCE path against a real Tally response.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger 3PM
nodes.notes: EDIT: confirm your n8n instance's timezone setting matches your business's local time, or the 3pm trigger will fire at the wrong local time.

nodes.name: Read Order Log
nodes.notes: Requires the Google Sheets credential attached in the n8n UI.

nodes.name: Filter To Today
nodes.notes: Keeps only rows logged today, and parses the JSON columns back into real arrays.

nodes.name: Aggregate Report Data
nodes.notes: Rolls up all of today's rows into the summary numbers for the report: order count, total raw materials to buy, total items to manufacture, total stock used.

nodes.name: Build Report Table Rows
nodes.notes: Flattens the report data into row objects that the Excel-conversion node can turn into a spreadsheet.

nodes.name: Convert To Excel
nodes.notes: EDIT: if your n8n version doesn't have 'Convert to File', use the older 'Spreadsheet File' node instead (n8n-nodes-base.spreadsheetFile) with the same xlsx settings.

nodes.name: Merge Excel And Summary
nodes.notes: Combines the binary Excel file with the HTML summary text so the Send Email node has both.

nodes.name: Send Report Email
nodes.notes: Requires an SMTP credential attached in the n8n UI (not stored in this export).

nodes.name: Merge BOM Result With Order Context
Order Webhook (From Website)
nodes.notes: Called by chemcorp's POST /api/orders right after an order is saved to Postgres. Expects { orderNumber, items: [{ product, qtyOrdered }, ...] }.

parameters.jsCode:
// Same best-effort Tally query shape as 'Build Tally Stock Query XML', for the BOM
// Explode subflow's item name field. NOT yet verified against a real Tally instance.
const companyName = "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_TALLY_COMPANY_NAME";
const itemName = item.json.itemName;

const tallyXmlQuery = `<ENVELOPE>
 <HEADER>
  <TALLYREQUEST>Export Data</TALLYREQUEST>
 </HEADER>
 <BODY>
  <EXPORTDATA>
   <REQUESTDESC>
    <REPORTNAME>Stock Summary</REPORTNAME>
    <STATICVARIABLES>
     <SVCURRENTCOMPANY>${companyName}</SVCURRENTCOMPANY>
     <SVSTOCKITEM>${itemName}</SVSTOCKITEM>
    </STATICVARIABLES>
   </REQUESTDESC>
  </EXPORTDATA>
 </BODY>
</ENVELOPE>`;

return { json: { ...item.json, tallyXmlQuery } };

// Best-effort standard Tally HTTP XML 'Import Data' Stock Journal voucher to deduct
// fulfilled quantity. Ledger/voucher-type conventions vary a lot between Tally setups -
// GODOWNNAME is a placeholder and this whole shape needs confirming against a real
// Tally import before it's trusted to actually write data.
const companyName = "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_TALLY_COMPANY_NAME";
const itemName = item.json.product;
const qty = item.json.fulfilledFromStock;
const date = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10).replace(/-/g, "");

const tallyDeductionXml = `<ENVELOPE>
 <HEADER>
  <TALLYREQUEST>Import Data</TALLYREQUEST>
 </HEADER>
 <BODY>
  <IMPORTDATA>
   <REQUESTDESC>
    <REPORTNAME>Vouchers</REPORTNAME>
    <STATICVARIABLES>
     <SVCURRENTCOMPANY>${companyName}</SVCURRENTCOMPANY>
    </STATICVARIABLES>
   </REQUESTDESC>
   <REQUESTDATA>
    <TALLYMESSAGE xmlns:UDF="TallyUDF">
     <VOUCHER VCHTYPE="Stock Journal" ACTION="Create">
      <DATE>${date}</DATE>
      <VOUCHERTYPENAME>Stock Journal</VOUCHERTYPENAME>
      <NARRATION>Auto-deducted for order ${item.json.orderNumber}</NARRATION>
      <ALLINVENTORYENTRIES.LIST>
       <STOCKITEMNAME>${itemName}</STOCKITEMNAME>
       <ISDEEMEDPOSITIVE>Yes</ISDEEMEDPOSITIVE>
       <ACTUALQTY>-${qty}</ACTUALQTY>
       <BILLEDQTY>-${qty}</BILLEDQTY>
       <GODOWNNAME>REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_GODOWN_NAME</GODOWNNAME>
      </ALLINVENTORYENTRIES.LIST>
     </VOUCHER>
    </TALLYMESSAGE>
   </REQUESTDATA>
  </IMPORTDATA>
 </BODY>
</ENVELOPE>`;

return { json: { ...item.json, tallyDeductionXml } };
